decisions.reason: Report cites index.js:3 inject=["apiProxy"] and index.js:9 ctx.apiProxy.llm.providers(), maps the break to A1-01 as the primary card, explains the host-plane fix (inject ["llm"] with listProviders plus listConfigurableProviders, matching the card's split row and field note), and explains the dead @deepseek-ai/dsh-host-apiproxy dependency at package.json:17 with the instruction to drop it since alpha.1 deletes the package — well beyond a bare card name.

The scan table accounts for all six non-hit categories with per-category pattern evidence and file citations. session-notes.js is correctly described as pure string/array utilities with no host coupling despite its filename, and cordis.patch.yml is classified as ordinary composition (a bundle insert row) rather than a host-source patch — the file is cited as existing, its insert is not misclassified, and no coupling is invented from names.

Section 4 explicitly concludes zero hits cannot establish compatibility, citing the scan's heuristic-only nature, curated card coverage, grep's blindness to data flow, and the unproven from-tag pin requiring dependency/runtime evidence; it clearly separates the decisive apiProxy blocker from the six negative categories, which it says only mean no carded migration work.

The report lists mandatory post-migration checks: build and typecheck against the target cohort, an isolated-profile cold boot with the entry active and no pending-service rows plus dump-config confirmation, and a real listProviders/listConfigurableProviders round covering success and failure — all framed as proposed steps explicitly not executed in the non-runnable static fixture.
